record.paper_title: Offline Reinforcement Learning: Tutorial, Review, and Perspectives on Open Problems
record.context_brief: Stable density-ratio and value estimation offline
record.original_question: Can the value-function estimators or state-marginal density-ratio estimators used to reduce the variance of importance-sampling methods be learned stably from a fully offline dataset, despite the out-of-distribution action queries introduced by dynamic programming? The setting is fixed-dataset offline reinforcement learning, where additional online data collection is unavailable and dynamic-programming corrections themselves may be unreliable outside the data distribution.

evidence.quote: The second challenge is that the most effective of these off-policy policy gradient methods either requires estimating the value function, or the state-marginal density ratios via dynamic programming. As several prior works have shown, and as we will review in Section 4, dynamic programming methods suffer from issues pertaining to out-of-distribution queries in completely offline settings, making it hard to stably learn the value function without additional corrections.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the fixed-dataset offline reinforcement learning setting. Let $M=(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{A},P,r,\gamma,\rho_0)$ be a Markov decision process with state space $\mathcal{S}$, action space $\mathcal{A}$, transition kernel $P(s'\mid s,a)$, reward function $r:\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{A}\to\mathbb{R}$, discount factor $\gamma\in[0,1)$, and initial-state distribution $\rho_0$. A learner is given only a static dataset $\mathcal{D}=\{(s_i,a_i,r_i,s'_i)\}_{i=1}^N$ of transitions sampled from some (unknown) behavior policy $\pi_\beta$, and is not permitted to interact further with the environment. For a target policy $\pi$, define:
- the state–action value function $Q^\pi(s,a)=\mathbb{E}_\pi[\sum_{t\ge 0}\gamma^t r(s_t,a_t)\mid s_0=s,a_0=a]$, and
- the discounted state-marginal density ratio $w^\pi(s)=d^\pi(s)/d^{\pi_\beta}(s)$, where $d^\pi$ denotes the (normalized) discounted state occupancy of $\pi$.

Importance-sampling estimators for off-policy policy evaluation and improvement can have their variance reduced by plugging in approximations $\widehat{Q}^\pi$ of $Q^\pi$ or $\widehat{w}^\pi$ of $w^\pi$. Standard ways to learn either object rely on dynamic-programming-style fixed-point updates (e.g., Bellman backups for $Q^\pi$ or stationary-distribution corrections such as DualDICE-type recursions for $w^\pi$); these updates evaluate the learned function at actions or states drawn from $\pi$ rather than from $\pi_\beta$, producing out-of-distribution queries that are not constrained by $\mathcal{D}$.

Problem. Devise an estimator $\widehat{Q}^\pi$ of $Q^\pi$ and/or an estimator $\widehat{w}^\pi$ of $w^\pi$, computable from $\mathcal{D}$ alone, that is provably stable—i.e., its training procedure converges and the resulting estimate satisfies a non-vacuous error bound (in an appropriate norm against $d^{\pi_\beta}$ or $d^\pi$) that does not blow up due to extrapolation of the function approximator on actions or states outside the support of the data distribution. Equivalently: identify general conditions on $(\mathcal{D},\pi,\pi_\beta,$ function class$)$ under which dynamic-programming-based learning of $Q^\pi$ or $w^\pi$ from a purely offline dataset can be made stable without requiring any additional online data collection, or show that no such procedure exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The stability of value-function and density-ratio estimation under purely offline data with out-of-distribution action queries remains an active research frontier. Subsequent work (e.g., conservative Q-learning, IQL, pessimistic value iteration, and offline DICE variants) provides partial remedies and finite-sample guarantees under coverage or concentrability assumptions, but no general method is known that guarantees stable estimation without such assumptions, so the question is regarded as open / partially addressed.

status_evidence.title: Offline Reinforcement Learning: Tutorial, Review, and Perspectives
status_evidence.snippet: Identifies stable offline value/density-ratio estimation under OOD queries as an open challenge.
status_evidence.claim: Problem is posed as an open challenge.

status_evidence.title: Conservative Q-Learning for Offline RL (Kumar et al., 2020)
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes a lower-bound Q-value learning procedure to mitigate OOD overestimation in offline RL.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress through pessimism, not a full solution.

status_evidence.title: Pessimistic Value Iteration for Offline RL (Jin, Yang, Wang, 2021)
status_evidence.snippet: Provides finite-sample suboptimality bounds for offline RL via pessimism, under partial coverage.
status_evidence.claim: Stability guarantees exist only under coverage-type assumptions.
